.

`--compose-model` and `--compose-secret` carry the deployment requirement
described under [Deployment support for model over
rides and secret\ngrants](#deployment-support-for-model-overrides-and-secret-grants): a launch that names\neither is refused befor

> [!WARNING]
>
> **With `--save-targets`, this ed
its the suite.** The composed environment is\n> appended to the suite's environment list, deliberately, because an\n> environment
the suite does not list is one nobody can re-run from the app\n> afterwards. Without it the stack is ephemeral and the suite is un
touched,\n> except on a deployment with no ephemeral-launch support, where a\n> single-target compose still attaches. The result r
eports both writes\n> (`composed.environment.created`, `composed.attachment.attached`) even when\n`--wait` it exits **4** (see the
exit-code table above). A per-target failure\ndoes not abort its siblings, so exiting 0 would let a pipeline read \"1 of 3\nruns

never started" as a clean launch.

#### `--file`: upload and run a suite file

`eval run --file` reads the versioned suite fi
le (`schemaVersion: \"1\"`),\nauthenticates, then validates. A contract-invalid file exits **2** after the\nauth request; it does

not start a run. `eval validate` on the same bytes
still exits 1: that command is a verdict on the file; this one is not.

The
file's `suite.id` is the declared suite identity. The first run creates a\nfile-owned suite stamped with that id; later runs of th
e same id in the same\nproject update that suite rather than creating a second one. A UI-authored\nsuite has no declared id, so no

file can claim it. Resolve is never by name.

File `passThreshold` is a fraction; the hosted suite grades on a percent. The
co
nversion refuses rather than approximates. A file count above **10**\n(`repetitions` in a `schemaVersion: \"1\"` file, `iterations

` in `"2"`) is
refused by name (`REPETITIONS_CAP`) and is not clamped.

**Which vocabulary the sync speaks is the deployment'
s call.** Before writing\nanything, the CLI reads `GET /capabilities` once. A deployment that advertises\n`vocabulary.version: 2`
gets every request with `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary: 2`\nand case bodies spelled canonically: `iterations` (the exact count),\n`lega
cyIterations` (the legacy floor, the same number) and `assertions`\ninstead of `repetitions` / `iterations` / `checks`. A deployme
nt without the\ncapability block, or without the capabilities route at all, is spoken to in\nvocabulary 1, byte-for-byte as before

. Nothing in the file changes either way:
the dialect of the file and the vocabulary of the wire are independent.

Cases are sy
nced in batches of at most 100 (`create_eval_cases`). Every\ndeclared case is created or updated, including `disabled: true` rows.
A case\nthe file **no longer declares** is deleted from the hosted suite before\nlaunch. A case the file still declares but marks
`disabled: true` is **kept,\nwith its history**; it is simply left out of the launch, so parking a flaky\ntest does not destroy i
ts past results and re-enabling it later resumes the\nsame case.\nThe run is scoped to the enabled cases either way. A file with n
o enabled\ncases is refused (`NO_ENABLED_CASES`) rather than launching the whole\npersisted suite. `--case` may only name an enabl
ed case. A later run updates\nexisting cases by declared id and creates new ones. An enabled case that\noverrides `passThreshold`
is refused: hosted grading is suite-wide. A\ndisabled case with the same override is ignored, matching how repetitions\nare checke
d. Authored\n`defaults.toolPolicy` and non-empty `defaults.validity` gates are refused at\nhosted CLI launch (`TOOL_POLICY_UNSUPPO
RTED` / the corresponding validity\nrefusal). Hosted platform-authored suites do not currently have a\ntool-policy field or enforc
ement path, so the CLI does not upload a suite that\nwould claim those guarantees. When supported by an eval runner, `toolPolicy`\
nis enforced at execution time with denied tools kept visible but blocked;\nserver annotations are advisory and **UNTRUSTED**. The
file's default count\n(`defaults.repetitions`, or `defaults.iterations` in `schemaVersion: \"2\"`) is\ninherited per case and is
not uploaded as a suite `minIterations` floor.\nAuthored `defaults.systemPrompt` and `defaults.temperature` are uploaded as\nexecu
tion defaults; omitted fields stay omitted so the platform applies its\nown defaults. `target.hosts` and `target.environment` are
attached before\nlaunch. A file environment takes precedence over file hosts for that launch,\nwhile an explicit CLI target takes
precedence over both. When an explicit CLI\ntarget is provided (for example `--host`), the file's `target.hosts` are\n**not** sync
hronized to the suite's persisted host attachments; the suite\nkeeps whatever hosts it already has. Host attachment synchronizatio
n only\nruns when no explicit CLI target overrides the file. Environment attachment\nsynchronization is unaffected and always runs

.

Without `--idempotency-key`, the CLI mints a fresh UUID for every invocation
and prints it to stderr before launch (`Eval id
empotency key: <key>`). Each\ninvocation therefore starts and bills a new run. To retry a launch whose\nresponse was lost (without
starting a second run), pass the key that was\nprinted: `--idempotency-key <printed-key>`. A replay is marked `deduped` in\nthe r

eceipt and human output. `--notes` is not part of the key.

##### Imported cases: live tool resolution, and per-run approval
Every file run performs the same live check `eval validate --project` performs,\n**before it writes anything**. It is not opt-in a

nd there is no flag to skip
it. A file with no deterministic `toolCall` steps asks no question and pays no
round trip.

What h

appens when a deterministic reference does not resolve depends on the
case:

| Case | Outcome |
| - | - |
| Selected (enabled
, and named by `--case` if you used it) | The launch **refuses before the suite is synced**: nothing is written and nothing is bil
led |\n| Imported, not selected | Its claim is rewritten to `unresolved` (keeping `sourceCaseKey`) and it is **still persisted**,
so the hosted record says what MCPJam found rather than still asserting a claim about a missing tool |\n| Native, not selected | L
eft exactly as authored. A hand-written case never acquires an `import` block from this: \"somebody wrote this\" and \"something c

onverted this" are different facts |

Each target is checked on **its own** server set. `--host` is checked against
that host'
s configured servers rather than the file's, because that is the set\nthe run connects: validating `target.servers` would approve
a tool the host\ncannot reach. A host the FILE declares uses its own `servers` list when it\ndeclares one (those are attached to t
he host before launch) and the host's\nconfigured set when the field is omitted. An explicitly empty `servers: []`\nis a real, emp
ty set (it clears the attachment before launch) and is\nvalidated as such, never as an omitted field. A step that pins `serverId`
ore the suite exists\n(`--all-targets`, `--compose-*`), or a host does not report a server set, or a\nhost pins a server the proje

ct no longer has, the launch refuses rather than
assuming the references are fine.

`--case` accepts a hosted row id, which doe
s not exist yet when this check\nruns. A selector this stage cannot map is therefore treated as possibly naming\nany enabled case,

so an unresolved reference still refuses; the launcher
resolves the selector itself a moment later.

A selected `approximated`

case refuses unless this invocation approves it:

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--allow-approximated <ca
se...>` | No | Approve an `approximated` imported case for **this run only**, by AUTHORED case id (`cases[].id`). Repeatable. `--f
ile` runs only |\n| `--approval-reason <text>` | With the above | Why the approximations are acceptable for this run. 1–500 charac
